sasha: Heads-up: onboarding OrpheusX-13B (row-wise int4) into staging showed a clear quality drop on news summarization compared to our fp16 baseline. Putting quick notes and actions here so infra/QA can follow.

jia: Can you paste the eval CLI and the main metrics?

sasha: Yep. Run (staging runner):
```
./eval_runner --model orpheusx-13b --quant int4-rowwise --prompts bench/news-summarize \
  --weights /mnt/models/orpheusx/step_4200/ --batch 16 --max-tokens 512 --seed 2026
```
Automation summary from eval-bot (2026-03-20T19:10Z):
- rouge1: fp16=0.418 -> int4=0.369
- rougeL: 0.393 -> 0.341
- BLEU4: 20.9 -> 17.8
- avg token logprob degraded ~0.08, ppl +6%
- median latency per request: +3ms (within noise)

matt: 4-5 pts on rouge1 is large. Any conversion notes?

sasha: Conversion was done with model-convert v2.1 (default runtime rotary params kept). After digging: upstream model_config.yaml lists rotary:
  base: 4096
  freq_scale: 0.97
but our conversion pipeline left rotary_base at default 10000 and freq_scale 1.0. Also we used our standard Unicode normalizer which strips invisible soft-hyphen (U+00AD).

omar: The soft-hyphen thing matters: training text used U+00AD as a visible line-wrap marker and many token boundaries in the vocab depend on it. Removing it causes token ID shifts for hyphenated compounds, which can misalign embeddings + cached KV lookups. I observed mismatched tokens while sampling: original token ids for "cross­section" -> ["cross­", "section"] vs our tokenizer -> ["crosssection"].

jia: Could both issues together cause the regression? Seems plausible. Which is cheaper to test?

matt: Adjusting rotary params at runtime is trivial, try that first with a small subset. If rotor change fixes majority, that wins. If not, try toggling normalizer to preserve U+00AD and re-build tokenizer.

sasha: Did a 250-example smoke: runtime rotary_base=4096 freq_scale=0.97 -> rouge1 0.369 -> 0.403 (partial recovery). Still ~0.015 shy of fp16.

omar: Good signal that rotary mismatch was a big chunk. Next: preserve soft-hyphen and run micro-eval. Note: if we change tokenizer, we must validate kv-cache alignment and streaming behavior (token shift changes client-side cached prefixes).

sasha: I pushed three artifact sets to S3:
- s3://redwood-staging/orpheusx/step_4200/artifacts/rotary-only-20260320.tar.gz
- s3://redwood-staging/orpheusx/step_4200/artifacts/preserve-softad-20260320.tar.gz
- s3://redwood-staging/orpheusx/step_4200/artifacts/combined-20260320.tar.gz
Also uploaded tokenizer diffs to the repo: https://redwood.internal/git/orpheusx/compare/tokenizer-preserve-softad

jia: Please open a ticket with run IDs and mark for eng-ml + eng-platform. We need a conversion-time check that flags non-default rotary params in model configs.

sasha: Created internal ticket #12402 and assigned to @matt and @omar. Includes quick-run ids: rot-only-515123, softad-515124, combined-515125. Link: https://redwood.internal/issue/12402

matt: If preserve-softad closes most of the gap, we should add a tokenizer-conversion flag and a simple tokenizer unit-test that runs a handful of training-era strings through both tokenizers and checks id parity.

omar: Agree. Also adding note: when changing tokenizer, run a short kv-cache regression test (our kv-checker harness) because even 1-token shifts can trigger different cache eviction ordering for long context requests.

eval-bot: follow-ups scheduled: run rot-only (job 515123) queued, preserve-softad (job 515124) queued, combined (job 515125) queued. Expected completion: 2026-03-21T03:00Z.

sasha: Will post final bench numbers when runs finish. Thanks all. :pray:
